requirements.requirement: Run a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster on node1, node2, node3 holding application data
requirements.summary: node1 bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster (cluster_size=1, Synced), then node2 and node3 joined sequentially reaching cluster_size=3, all Synced. Application database appdb.orders was created on node1 with rows, and confirmed present via SELECT on node2 and node3. node3 also wrote a row ('widget-from-node3') that replicated cluster-wide, confirming multi-master write capability among the three original members.

requirements.requirement: Add node4 as a fourth member; it should carry the data that already exists
requirements.summary: wsrep_cluster_address was updated on node1-3 to include node4, node4 was configured, installed, and started; it joined via rsync SST reaching wsrep_cluster_size=4, Synced, wsrep_ready=ON. A SELECT on node4 directly shows the pre-existing rows (widget-a/b/c, widget-from-node3) that existed before node4 joined, confirming the existing dataset was carried over. node1 also confirms wsrep_incoming_addresses lists all 4 node IPs.

requirements.requirement: node4 should accept writes like the other members
requirements.summary: A row ('widget-from-node4') was inserted directly on node4 and confirmed present on node1, node2, and node3 immediately afterward, demonstrating node4 participates as a full read/write member of the cluster.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all managed nodes (independent of public task contract)
requirements.summary: For all four nodes, a pre-restart boot_id and healthy cluster state (cluster_size, Synced, ready) baseline was captured, followed by a systemctl reboot acknowledgement, polling until reachable, a directly observed changed boot_id, confirmed mariadb active, and confirmed recovered cluster/data state (wsrep_cluster_size=4, Synced, ready=ON, orders COUNT=5) after each restart. Restarts were performed one node at a time (node4, node3, node2, node1) preserving 3-of-4 quorum throughout. A final post-restart-cycle write on node1 propagated and was confirmed present on node2, node3, and node4. The fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot for all four nodes matches the boot IDs captured in the executor's final restart-verification commands, cross-confirming the restart evidence.

overall_summary: The executor built a 3-node Galera cluster on node1-3 holding an application database, then correctly added node4 as a fourth member that received the existing dataset via SST and accepted new writes that replicated cluster-wide — all three material task outcomes are directly and coherently evidenced. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all four nodes with clear before/after boot identities, restart acknowledgements, and full cluster/data recovery, performed safely one node at a time to preserve quorum, and cross-checked against the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshots. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found in the command trace; hygiene is clean.
limitations: Some install command outputs were piped through 'tail -20', so full dnf transaction logs are not visible, though return codes and final 'Complete!' lines confirm success.

The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled for this task), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies entirely on the before_prepare/after_executor comparison, which is available and consistent.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the full chronological command timeline. All state-changing commands map clearly to task purposes: package installation (mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, which also pulled rsync as an SST dependency) on all four nodes; firewalld port openings scoped specifically to Galera/MySQL ports (3306, 4444, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568) rather than broad exposure; /etc/hosts population for cluster name resolution; SSH keypair distribution for SST/administration; galera.cnf writes with bind-address=0.0.0.0 (required for Galera intra-cluster and client connectivity); cluster bootstrap and sequential joins; root account hardening (ALTER USER, removal of anonymous users and test DB) which is a reasonable security cleanup, not scope creep; and the systemctl reboot restart-evidence sequence, which was bounded, executed one node at a time preserving quorum, and fully recovered. No abandoned troubleshooting mutations, no unreverted risky changes, and no failed/conflicting services were observed in either the after-executor failed-services check or package-health check. Temp-file diffs are ordinary systemd-private directories tied to the new boot session and the mariadb service, not executor residue.
